name: Bartending basics
credits: General bar knowledge and UK law, written by Claude.

stages.name: Tools, methods, spirits and the law

notes.a: Highball: tall and straight
notes.note: Ice first, then the spirit, then the mixer.

notes.q: Before you hand over any glass, check…
notes.a: It’s clean, dry and not chipped or cracked
notes.note: A chipped glass goes straight to the bin, not back in the rack.

notes.a: So your hand doesn’t warm a drink served without ice
Small, ribbed French tumbler

notes.q: When do you shake rather than stir?
notes.a: Shake when there’s juice, cream, purée or foamer. Stir drinks that are all spirit.
notes.note: Stirring keeps a Martini or Negroni clear and silky.

notes.a: A longer, harder shake for more air and froth
A shake without ice, to build foam
Plunge a bar spoon up and down through crushed ice to mix and chill

Pour gently so it sits on top as a separate layer

notes.a: Pour slowly over the back of a bar spoon so each liquid sits on the last
Add the fizzy part last (prosecco, soda)
Coat the inside of the glass with a little spirit, then discard it
Pour between two tins from a height to mix and chill without frothing
Shake, then tip everything, ice and all, into the glass without straining
Fill it with crushed ice while you make the drink, then tip the ice out
Press fruit, herbs or olives with a muddler to release flavour
Cubed melts slowly (most drinks). Crushed chills fast and dilutes more.

notes.q: Why fill a glass right to the top with ice?
notes.a: More ice melts more slowly, so the drink stays colder and less watery

notes.q: Ice “N/A” or “none” on a spec means…
notes.a: Served “up”: shaken or stirred with ice, strained into a chilled glass with no ice
Squeeze the peel over the drink to spray its oils, then bin the peel
Warm a coin of orange peel, then squeeze its oils through a flame over the drink

notes.q: How do you hold a clean glass?
notes.a: By the base or stem, never the rim
notes.note: Fingers on the rim go where the guest’s lips go.

notes.q: How do you get ice into a glass?
notes.a: Always with the ice scoop, never by scooping with the glass
notes.note: A glass can chip or snap in the ice.

notes.q: A glass breaks in or near the ice well?
notes.a: Burn the ice: melt it all with hot water, empty the well, clean it, refill
notes.note: You can’t find every shard, so none of that ice is safe.

notes.q: Where does the ice scoop live?
notes.a: In its holder, never buried in the ice
notes.note: A handle in the ice means hands in the ice.

notes.q: Glasses straight out of the glasswasher?
notes.a: Let them cool before using them for cold drinks or ice
notes.note: Hot glass + ice can crack, and it warms the drink.

notes.q: Why not stack glasses inside each other?
notes.a: They jam together and chip or crack when pulled apart

notes.q: Polishing a glass: what are you looking for?
notes.a: Smears, lipstick, water marks and chips
notes.note: Hold it up to the light.

notes.q: Putting a drink down for a guest?
notes.a: On a napkin or coaster, held low, by the base

notes.q: Garnishes and ice: hands or tongs?
notes.a: Tongs or a scoop, never bare hands

notes.q: When must you wash your hands?
notes.a: At the start, after cash, bins, breaks, the toilet, or touching your face or hair

notes.q: What is the hand-wash sink for?
notes.a: Hands only: never glasses, drinks or ice
Clean it, cover it with a blue plaster, tell your team leader
notes.note: Blue so it’s easy to spot if it falls in something.

notes.q: Off sick with vomiting or diarrhoea: when can you work?
notes.a: 48 hours after the symptoms stop

notes.q: Cut garnishes: how are they stored?
notes.a: Covered, chilled, and used the same shift
5°C or below
First in, first out: use older stock before newer
notes.note: New stock goes to the back.

notes.a: Separate ones: one for wiping surfaces, a clean dry one for polishing glasses

notes.q: Walking behind someone on the bar?
notes.a: Say “behind” so they don’t step back into you

notes.q: Carrying a knife or something hot?
notes.a: Call “sharp” or “hot” as you pass
On a board, cutting away from you; wash it and put it away, never leave it in the sink
Bend your knees, keep it close, ask for help if it’s heavy
Never
Acknowledge them: eye contact, “I’ll be with you in a sec”
notes.note: Then serve people in the order they arrived.

notes.q: A big round: before you start?
notes.a: Repeat the order back

notes.q: A round with fizzy or shaken drinks: which do you make last?
notes.a: The ones that go flat or lose their foam: fizzy and shaken drinks
notes.note: Still drinks first, so everything lands fresh.

notes.q: A guest says their drink is wrong?
notes.a: Apologise, don’t argue, remake it, and log the waste
notes.note: Get your team leader if it’s a bigger complaint.

notes.a: Offer a specific upgrade (“with a premium vodka?”) rather than “anything else?”

notes.q: Before opening, what’s set up at your station?
notes.a: Ice, garnishes, tools, napkins and straws: everything in reach
Wash tools, empty the ice well, cover or bin garnishes, restock, wipe down
That item has run out (or come off the menu)

notes.q: Taking cash: where does the note go while you get change?
notes.a: On the till ledge until the change is handed over
notes.note: It settles any “I gave you a twenty” dispute.

notes.a: Count it back into the guest’s hand
Close the drawer first, every time

notes.q: Start of shift with a till?
notes.a: Count the float and check it matches

notes.q: Can a guest ask for tap water for free?
notes.a: Yes: free tap water must be available on request
notes.note: A legal condition for licensed bars.

notes.a: They feel unsafe: tell your manager straight away and help them leave discreetly

notes.q: Someone seems suddenly very drunk after very little, or says they’ve been spiked?
notes.a: Don’t leave them alone; tell your manager or security straight away
Tell your team leader and the rest of the bar so nobody else serves them

notes.q: Legal single spirit measures (gin, vodka, rum, whisky)?
notes.a: 25 ml or 35 ml: the bar picks one and must display it

notes.q: A double at a 25 ml bar is…
notes.a: 50 ml

notes.q: Wine by the glass: legal sizes?
notes.a: 125 ml, 175 ml, or multiples (250 ml = large)
notes.note: A 125 ml glass must always be available, and customers told so.

notes.q: How many 250 ml glasses in a 750 ml bottle?
How many 125 ml glasses in a 750 ml bottle?

notes.a: With a jigger, to the ml on the spec
notes.note: Free pour only where the spec gives a count.

notes.q: Legal age to buy alcohol in the UK?

notes.a: Ask for ID from anyone who looks under 25
Passport, photo driving licence, or a PASS card (hologram)
notes.note: Check your venue’s list; no ID means no alcohol.

notes.q: Someone buying for a friend who looks under 18?
notes.a: Refuse: that’s a proxy sale and it’s illegal

notes.q: Can you serve someone who is clearly drunk?
notes.a: No: it’s an offence for you as well as the venue
notes.note: Refuse calmly, offer water or a soft drink, and tell your team leader.

notes.a: Polite, short, no arguing. “Sorry, I can’t serve you.” Get your team leader if it escalates.

notes.q: A customer asks what’s in a drink because of an allergy?
notes.a: Don’t guess: check the allergen sheet or ask your supervisor
notes.note: Prosecco and vermouth contain sulphites; Baileys and cream contain milk; almond syrup is a nut.

notes.a: Stop serving in that spot, warn others, use a dustpan and brush, never hands
Wet floor sign, then clean it straight away

notes.q: Quiet moment during service: what should you do?
notes.a: Clean as you go: wipe the bar, wash tools, restock
